- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) or trending negative, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to cap peak — reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days to reflect mean reversion.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.6) and price is rising, model frequently overestimates continuation — cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use sentiment-weighted moving average.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.3–0.5) — add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for hidden momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates final 5–7 days — apply a “late-stage bias” correction: add 0.5–1.5% to last 3–5 forecast points if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment drops sharply (e.g., from 0.7 to 0.1) within 3 days, model often fails to anticipate reversal — add 1–2% upward bias to compensate for lagged sentiment effect.
